explanation.body:
Conditional convergence evaluates if the given alternating series converges ONLY as an alternating series. 
Series $(i)$ is a geometric series whose $r$ value is less than 1, so the series converges absolutely. Absolute convergence and conditional convergence are mutually exclusive, so Series $(i)$ is excluded from our possibilities. 
Series $(ii)$ is a p-series whose p value is less than 1. Thus, under normal circumstances, $(ii)$ would diverge. However, because it is alternating and its terms go to 0, the series converges conditionally. 
Series $(iii)$ would diverge under normal conditions. However, the terms still go to zero and the series alternates, so the series converges conditionally.
